- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% if recent price is trending up.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply “lag correction”: reduce forecast by 5–10% for 2–4 days after peak.  
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, apply “mean reversion bias”: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day from forecast until price stabilizes.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often overfits recent volatility; use 10–15% smoothing on forecast to reduce noise.  
- If true outcome is below 70% of historical mean, model tends to overreact; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent low.
